conclusion: Original-host memory loss after confirmed cleanup is preventable by an independently persisted signed host exit receipt. Death before any trustworthy cleanup observation remains unknowable, not force-recoverable.

implementation.storage: Existing host data root/workflow-v3-exits, outside project workspace; existing parent is resolved and outside-project location verified before creating receipt directory. Reads do not create directories.
implementation.authority: Existing BEEGAME_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY, HMAC domain-separated derivation. Key not written into receipt, user request or normal native environment; no new settings/hooks/key provisioning. Root environment presence checked without displaying key.
implementation.publication: Write exclusive temporary file, fsync bytes, atomically link final immutable receipt without replacing prior proof, fsync directory. Partial .tmp files are not accepted. Current-platform process-death durability verified, not whole-disk/power-loss or universal OS guarantees.
persistedFacts: Question provenance where existing executor observes it
implementation.recovery: Existing authenticated explicit recover-writer API, current CAS version/owner/writer identity and no-active-writer guards. Restore factual quiescence then mark interrupted/failed; preserve paused intent, requirements, saved bytes and unrelated results. Never automatically dispatch.
implementation.readApi: recoveryEvidence adds host-receipt; hostExitReceiptsConfigured reports configured capability. Corrupt or unusable records show unavailable; explicit recovery reports exit-receipt-invalid.
implementation.writeFailure: Log sanitized local-receipt warning and retain original-host observation; do not block normal DB quiescence/settlement solely because optional local copy fails.
implementation.legacy: Compatible Task/source-save path shares same receipt helper; no new stage, migration, supervisor, heartbeat, takeover or engine/renderer selection.

limitations: No real remote SQL/RPC experiment this round.
Actual SIGKILL uses fake native transport; real CLI path uses app reconstruction, not SIGKILL. Separate layers are not claimed as one combined real-model/remote-DB crash acceptance.
No real game, design judgment, engine or subjective quality acceptance.
initialHarnessFailures: First receipt test child stdin used end(payload), which did not write bytes in Bun; corrected write then end.
Source fixture lacked required entryScene/scene registry and typed draft narrowing; fixture corrected, production validation unchanged.
Optional Buffer assertion types corrected without weakening byte checks.
Compatible task test initially disposed immediately before native start; corrected to await actual exit-persistence checkpoint.
Package-level tsc command resolved wrong aliases and reported unrelated core errors; root project typecheck is the verified command.
Unescalated tests could not listen on loopback; same regressions passed with local network permission, without assertion relaxation.

remaining: Old unknown writers without database proof or signed host receipt remain locked; no invented migration/backfill.
Host dies before owned cleanup/receipt publication: no factual recovery proof. PID/time/session-terminal/user claims remain insufficient.
Loss of trusted host disk, signature key or different machine without receipt storage remains unavailable.
Receipt establishes owned host quiescence only, not completion of all remote MCP/paid/Unity/Godot operations; uncertain external outcomes unaccepted and not retried.
Same-OS malicious actor with host secret or host process compromise can defeat trust; signature is not full OS isolation.
Root config key rotation invalidates old host receipts until actual DB proof is available; no automatic key fallback or keyring framework.
Local receipts retained; no automatic historical deletion or rewritten proof.
Real remote deployment combination, historical 1.75 downloaded ZIP identity, eight-domain design/resources/Scene/UI/game quality and actual engine delivery remain unaccepted.
Formal frontend and publishing excluded, costs last, no token savings claimed.
